reviewMethod: Independent visual inspection of all 16 original paper pages and scheme PDF pages 29–52, including every model solution, alternative method, diagram, scale, shared component allocation and detailed credit note. All 31 question and 31 solution crops visually inspected.
sourceNotes: All 16 paper pages and scheme pages 29–52 independently visually inspected; page 16 is extra work and scheme pages 51–52 contain no additional tasks.
Both Q6A and Q6B retained: 325 offered marks versus 300 candidate marks.
Shared scales: Q2(b,c,d), Q3(c,d), Q4(b,c), Q7(g,h), Q8(b)(i,ii). All required prompts retained in each holistic card.
Q1 examples and Q2(a) constructed outcomes are responses, not a printed finite menu of alternative questions. The model examples do not restrict valid answers.
Required lists, both slopes, both intercepts and both Q6B(b) angles remain complete within their published tariffs.
Original data, stem-and-leaf key, histograms, constructions, alternative methods and complete detailed marking notes retained.
The 25B* Q8(a)(ii) allocation is unusual but agrees in summary and detailed notes. Only three tasks are starred.
Source notes explain the Q3(b) mean decimal, Q7(b) vertical scale, and Q8(b) premature-rounding difference.

cards.questionText: Give an example of an experiment with two outcomes that are equally likely, stating clearly what the two outcomes are.
cards.markingNote: The experiment and both outcomes form one response. The coin experiment is an example, not the only permitted answer.

cards.questionText: Give an example of an experiment with two outcomes that are not equally likely, stating clearly what the two outcomes are.
cards.markingNote: The experiment and both outcomes form one response. The model experiments are examples; an appropriate sample space can make an apparently incorrect example valid.

cards.stem: A girl and a boy each think of a whole number from 1 to 10. Record the outcome as an ordered pair: for example, (3, 1) means the girl picks 3 and the boy picks 1.
cards.questionText: Write out three possible outcomes of this experiment.
cards.markingNote: Give three distinct valid ordered pairs. This is example construction, not selection from a printed menu of alternative questions. All three examples share one 20C award; the SEC examples are illustrative.

cards.stem: A girl and a boy each think of a whole number from 1 to 10. Record the outcome as an ordered pair: for example, (3, 1) means the girl picks 3 and the boy picks 1.
cards.questionText: (b) How many different outcomes are there? (c) Write all outcomes where the children pick the same number. (d) If all numbers are equally likely and the choices independent, what is the probability of the same number?
cards.markingNote: All three printed parts share one five-mark scale. Complete all three for full credit. Part (d) correct, or both (b) and (c) correct, earns high partial credit. All ten equal-number pairs are required in (c).

cards.markingNote: The original model accepts 9 assuming a uniform distribution within the first class, or 7/8 using a smoother overall distribution. Keep the estimate consistent in later calculations.

cards.markingNote: The population estimate and explanation of uncertainty share one five-mark scale. Both parts are required for full credit; either complete part earns high partial credit. Use the candidate’s consistent sample estimate, not only the model’s 9 out of 200.

cards.markingNote: The original scheme accepts either a supported comparison or a cautious response about random variation. Both original explanations are retained; the same five marks apply.

cards.stem: An isosceles triangular earring is half copper and half silver. Its base is 2 cm and perpendicular height 4 cm; the sloping side is d and its base angle is α.
cards.questionText: (i) Use Pythagoras’ theorem to find d, to one decimal place. (ii) Find α, to the nearest degree.
cards.markingNote: The length and angle share one five-mark scale. Both are required for full credit; either complete part earns high partial credit. All three trigonometric methods are retained.

cards.stem: An isosceles triangular earring is half copper and half silver. Its base is 2 cm and perpendicular height 4 cm; the sloping side is d and its base angle is α.

cards.markingNote: The original earring dimensions and half-silver design are retained as prerequisites. The enlarged base is 4 cm and height 8 cm.
